SWE-2011-28 African urban agriculture: social, economic and environmental challenges and prospects under changing global and demographic realitie

description.narrative: Urbanization rates in Africa are increasing rapidly, while rising food prices and domestic climate change effects are likely to make feeding urban areas more problematic even in the near future. In this context, urban agriculture (UA) appears to be taking on an increasingly important role as a source of food and income. Nonetheless, the social, economic and environmental effects of UA, especially in intermediate sized urban areas are poorly understood. The project uses a multi-disciplinary mixed-methods approach combining household level interviews and survey data with collection of soil and water samples in eight urban areas in Ghana and Kenya to investigate how how UA influences household food security and welfare, whether differences based on socio-economic status and gender can be found in patterns of UA, and the health related consequences of UA.
